does_not_cover: Never computes a test statistic from raw data: no t-value, no critical-value lookup, no z-test walkthrough; the 0.03/0.06 p-values arrive pre-made.
Title promises how to choose tails but never shows a case where a one-sided test is legitimate; every example ends in 'always two-sided'.
notes: Brisk pacing, single running clinical-trial example; p-hacking/false-positive material touches l10-multiple only in passing, not taught. No notation clashes; thin by design at 7 minutes.

segments.topic: Clinical-trial setup: one-sided p 0.03 versus two-sided p 0.06
What each tail choice actually hypothesizes
Decide tails before the experiment or it is p-hacking
Simulation: 10,000 two-sided t-tests and the 5% false positives
Switching to one-sided after peeking pushes errors to 8%
Recommendation: default to two-sided whenever a choice exists

suggested_locator: 01:52-02:38 for the meaning of each choice; 05:08-06:02 for the peeking-inflates-errors demo

teaches.why: Contrasts one- vs two-sided p-values on one dataset and defines each hypothesis.
Demonstrates false-positive rate 5% vs 8% via a 10,000-test simulation.
